city.name: Stillwater
city.description: A post-industrial river city of about 40,000. Its kilns and dye works closed decades ago; its economy now turns on a single automated logistics centre, a council tower and a long tail of care, retail and gig work. Public services are coordinated from the Council Tower, whose predictive systems schedule buses, allocate housing and set patrol routes. The river runs slow and brown through Lowbank. Officially, nothing much happens in Stillwater.

districts.name: Council Hill
districts.description: Civic core on the rise above the river: the Council Tower, police station, magistrates' court and the old Carnegie library around a paved forecourt.

districts.name: Mercer Row
districts.description: The commercial spine: covered market, pawnbrokers, cafes, off-licences and the central transit interchange.

districts.name: Ashgrove
districts.description: Terraced and semi-detached owner-occupied streets around a Victorian park and the primary school.

districts.name: Kiln Works
districts.description: Former brick and dye works, now dominated by the Halden fulfilment centre, scrapyards and lorry parks.

districts.name: Lowbank
districts.description: Flood-prone riverside streets: the Weir Court towers, the night shelter, the community clinic and the River Lane underpass.

districts.name: Fallow Edge
districts.description: Peripheral 1970s estate on the ring road, poorly served by transit, bordered by allotments and fields.

residents.name: Marcus Hale
residents.citizen_bio: Marcus spent twelve years keeping Stillwater's parcels moving and still knows every aisle at Halden by heart.

residents.name: Dorothy Pryce
residents.citizen_bio: Dot is a familiar face at the Carnegie Library, where she has been known to reshelve the large-print section unasked.

residents.name: Kayleigh Doyle
residents.citizen_bio: Kayleigh brings tea and good humour to Lowbank's elderly residents on her daily care rounds.

residents.name: Sunil Varma
residents.citizen_bio: Sunil has driven every road in Stillwater and is Fallow Edge's most tireless letter-writer.

residents.name: Jordan Reece
residents.citizen_bio: Jordan is a Lowbank lad with fast hands and a faster laugh, looking for his next start.

residents.name: Terrence Lusk
residents.household: Lives alone; estranged daughter and grandson
residents.citizen_bio: Terry has lived in Fallow Edge for thirty years and can fix any bicycle you bring him.

residents.name: Elena Marsh
residents.citizen_bio: Elena led the automation programme that made Halden one of the most efficient fulfilment centres in the region.

residents.name: Daniel Marsh
residents.citizen_bio: Mr Marsh has taught a generation of Ashgrove seven-year-olds to read, and still runs the park loop three times a week.

residents.name: Mia Marsh
residents.citizen_bio: Mia pours the best flat white on Mercer Row and volunteers Sundays at St Brigid's.

residents.name: Walter Greaves
residents.citizen_bio: Walter and his late wife Margaret were married 58 years; you will find him on her bench in Ashgrove Park most mornings.

residents.name: Priya Anand
residents.citizen_bio: Priya keeps the Carnegie open, warm and curious, and will find you any book you can half-remember.

residents.name: Callum Shore
residents.citizen_bio: Callum's forecasting work keeps Halden's deliveries, and Stillwater's shelves, right on time.
